claim: A native story built through an imported alias or factory-made `story` is dropped, though the same code in-file stays in
A top-level var redeclared with a value inside a block or a for…of/for…in head is not counted as an assignment, so the name is treated as never reassigned

triage.scenario: `var meta = { title: 'A' }; if (flag) { var meta = { title: 'B' }; }` or `var s = X; for (var s of list) {}`. Each nested `var` with an initializer, and each `for (var x of …)` head, assigns the same top-level binding. `assignedNames` only counts `=`, `++` and `for` heads that are not a VariableDeclaration, and the top-level declaration of the name hides nothing. So `bindingsOf` keeps the first initializer as the binding's value, and `objectOf`/`stringOf` read a title, component or isolate value the module may not hold at runtime. Expected: the binding is treated as reassigned and bound to its declarator.
triage.cause: var declarators with init below top level not counted as assignments

claim: foreignStories caches the depth-limit answer by key, so the result depends on the order imports are visited
A capture's cache key leaves out the origins it was allowed to load, so captures that allow different origins share one cache entry

triage.scenario: `allowOrigins` is a thunk "read at each capture", so it can change while the server runs. A payload captured while a font or image origin was not allowed renders without it, and its PNG is cached under `keyOf(payload)`. After the allowlist changes, the same payload is served from the cache with the blocked resource still missing until some client module edit calls `revise()`. The key should include `allowOrigins()`, or a change to the allowlist should clear the cache.
triage.cause: cache key omits a render input

claim: componentOf does not see through a TypeScript cast: an identifier inside a cast in objectOf, or a cast or call inside a spread in componentIn, is not followed where the babel indexer follows it

triage.scenario: `const meta = { component: Button }; export default meta satisfies Meta<typeof Button>;`. Because the default export is not a bare identifier, TS creates no alias symbol for it. Its declaration is an ExportAssignment whose expression is a SatisfiesExpression. The loop unwraps that to the Identifier `meta` and then gives up, since Identifier is neither an object literal, a call, nor a cast. `assigned` returns undefined, so the args table loses the component, or `metaComponentOf` reads the `Meta` type's `component` and gets `any` props. In the same way, a spread `...(base as Meta)` or `...meta({ component: X })` in componentIn goes through `getSymbolAtLocation` on a non-identifier expression, which yields no symbol, so the component the spread carries is dropped. The babel side (`ast.ts` objectOf/lookup) follows identifiers through casts and wrapper calls in both positions, so the indexer's `componentName` and the TS-side component disagree.
triage.cause: identifier/cast/call not unwrapped in TS-side object resolution

claim: The component graph and the API table give different answers for a dotted `component` off a named import

triage.scenario: `import * as h from './storyHelpers'` where storyHelpers has `export { meta } from '@weasel-js/forge'`, and the story file does `export default h.meta({ component: Button })`. `foreignCallees` (indexFile.ts:73-79) reports `h.meta` as a namespace-member callee, the wrapper resolver finds forge's `meta` behind it, and the indexer treats the file as native. `isForgeWrapper` only accepts a namespace import whose own specifier is `@weasel-js/forge` (`fromForge(d)` on the NamespaceImport), so `objectOf` stops at the call, `assigned` finds no `component`, and `componentOf`/`metaComponentOf` fall back to the title stand-in or the meta type's `component` property (props `any`). The same happens for a named import from a helper that does `export * from '@weasel-js/forge'`: `getImmediateAliasedSymbol` jumps straight to forge's own declaration and never meets a specifier whose text is `@weasel-js/forge`, so the loop ends false. The doc comment says "The story indexer reads no other call as a meta, so neither does this", but the indexer reads both cases. Expected: one answer for whether a callee is forge's `meta`/`story`. Actual: the args table and the component graph get a different component from the one the index reports (or none).
triage.cause: wrapper check reimplemented narrower than the indexer's resolver

claim: The component's own file, read for destructured defaults, is not recorded in `sources`

A stylesheet's relative `url(font.woff2)` behind a CDN redirect breaks the same way, and the capture renders without that dependency or with a missing font. The screen, which follows the redirect natively, renders correctly, so the capture differs from what the screen shows.

claim: The props table and the dependency graph pick different components for the same story file
passThrough never consumes or cancels a redirect hop's response body

triage.scenario: an allowlisted origin answers with a 30x carrying a body (most servers send a short HTML body). The loop reads `location` and `continue`s without `response.body?.cancel()` or reading the body, and it does the same on the `reach` abort path. undici holds the connection and its buffers until the body is consumed or garbage-collected. A story whose assets redirect, captured repeatedly, ties up keep-alive sockets to that origin; the next hop or capture to the same origin can stall behind them until GC runs. Every hop should cancel the body it drops.
triage.cause: unconsumed fetch body

claim: The name-rev --refs pattern lets a package's version be read from another package's tag whose name has a path segment starting with a digit or v+digit

claim: A capture queued when the endpoint closes relaunches Chromium after close

triage.scenario: a graph has been sent once (`depsSent !== null`); a page reloads (or a second tab opens) and requests `deps.js`, so `module()` starts building and reads file F. F is edited: the plugin invalidates F and calls `redeps`, which, since `depsSent !== null`, starts `rebuild` concurrently instead of recording `editedWhileServing`. The rebuild reads the new F, sets `depsSent = G1` and pushes `forge:deps` G1. Then `module()` finishes with the graph it built from the old F, overwrites `depsSent = G0` and serves G0; the page's `import('virtual:forge/deps.js').then(setDependencies)` lands after the push and replaces G1 with G0. The page shows the stale graph, and because `depsSent` now equals G0, nothing re-pushes until a later edit happens to change the graph again. Should: an edit during `module()` always schedules a rebuild after it is served (the `editedWhileServing` path), whatever `depsSent` holds, or `module()` should not overwrite a `depsSent` written by a rebuild that started after it.
triage.cause: edit-while-serving recorded only when nothing was sent yet
